sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mongfhinn, also spelled Mongfhin and Mongfhionn, was an Irish heroine. Her name served as a charm to keep away evil spirits. Yet Mongfhinn herself was not especially pleasant. She was stepmother or foster mother to Niall of the Nine Hostages. She tried to poison him. Instead she killed herself on Samhain night, the feast that starts winter on November 1. In some parts of Ireland that holiday was called the Festival of Monghfinn. This obscure figure may once have been an important goddess. Her name carries the divine syllable fionn, which means light. Women once prayed to her on Samhain.

okr.objective: Document the Irish heroine Mongfhinn and her Samhain links.
